title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed announced that TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not be published on Friday, April 3, 2026 due to the March Employment Situation report release and the resulting non-closure of government securities markets, which disrupts cleared Treasury repo settlement—the basis for two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates. These rates will be published on Monday, April 6, reflecting Thursday-to-Monday repo transactions. EFFR and OBFR will still be published on April 3 per the Fed's regular holiday schedule.
key_points: No publication of TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, or SOFR Averages/Index on Friday, April 3, 2026
Absence of cleared Treasury repo settlement eliminates two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates
On Monday April 6, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR will be published reflecting same-day settling Treasury repo transactions settling Thursday April 2 and maturing Monday April 6
SOFR Averages and Index published April 6 will have a value date of April 6
EFFR and OBFR publication follows NY Fed holiday schedule and will be published on Friday April 3
Repo market participants broadly expect to treat April 3 as a holiday despite SIFMA not recommending full market closure
why_it_matters: This operational notice affects the integrity and timing of SOFR-based markets. Market participants who rely on SOFR as a reference rate for derivatives, loans, or risk calculations will face a gap in published rates. The disruption to cleared Treasury repo settlement means the most robustly calculated Treasury repo reference rates (TGCR/BGCR) cannot be computed. This is relevant for anyone with floating-rate exposures, valuation models, or collateral desks that depend on daily SOFR publication.
market_structure_context: The notice highlights market plumbing dependencies: SOFR and related Treasury repo reference rates depend on cleared repo settlement availability. When cleared Treasury repo settlement is unavailable, two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo rates are eliminated, preventing same-day publication. This underscores the interdependency between data release calendars, SIFMA holiday recommendations, and critical overnight rate calculations. EFFR and OBFR use a different calculation methodology not dependent on cleared repo settlement, allowing them to publish on schedule.
